name: 瞳孔不安定指数解析
description: Measures pupillary unrest (hippus) — natural pupil oscillations absent in AI-generated faces.
algorithm: Pupillary Unrest Index分析アルゴリズム
mechanism:
This method analyzes pupillary unrest (hippus) for deepfake detection:

1. **瞳孔Size測定**: Pupil diameter is measured per frame using iris-pupil boundary detection and ellipse fitting. High-resolution tracking captures the temporal signal of pupil diameter changes.

2. **Hippus検出**: Pupillary unrest (hippus) is the continuous, involuntary oscillation of pupil diameter at frequencies of 0.5-2 Hz with amplitude of 0.2-0.5mm. This is a normal physiological phenomenon reflecting sympathetic-parasympathetic nervous system interplay. The method checks for the presence and characteristics of hippus.

3. **Pupillary光Reflex**: When illumination changes, pupils should constrict (light increase) or dilate (light decrease) with characteristic latency (~200ms) and dynamics (rapid constriction, slower dilation). The method checks for correct pupillary light reflex dynamics. Deepfakes typically don't model this physiological response.

4. **Bilateral瞳孔Coordination**: Both pupils should show consensual response — constricting/dilating together with minimal difference (≤0.5mm). The method checks bilateral pupil size correlation. AI generators may produce independent pupil sizes between left and right eyes, violating the consensual pupil response.

5. **Cognitive瞳孔Response**: Cognitive effort and emotional arousal produce small pupil dilations (0.1-0.5mm above baseline). The method analyzes whether pupil size correlates with speech content complexity and emotional context. Deepfake pupils that don't respond to cognitive demands lack this natural physiological signal.
parameters: 分析タイプ：自動統計\nスコア範囲：0（本物）から100（AI生成）
accuracy: 中〜高 — 入力品質に応じて70-85%の精度。
source: デジタルフォレンジックとAIコンテンツ検出の査読済み研究に基づく。
useCase: AI生成コンテンツを検出するためのマルチシグナル分析パイプラインの一部として使用。
strengths: • 研究に裏付けられた方法論\n• 高速な計算時間\n• 他の検出方法と相補的
limitations: • 精度は入力品質により変動\n• 他の方法と組み合わせて使用するのが最適

references.title: Ciftci, U.A. et al. (2020). FakeCatcher: Detection of Synthetic Portrait Videos Using Biological Signals. IEEE TPAMI.
